title: Scout
headline: I built an AI analyst that answered a revenue team's questions in Slack
summary: A Slack bot built with Claude Code that read the data warehouse and affiliate offer feeds, and answered with how sure it was and one next step.
description: An AI analyst in Slack that answered a revenue team's data questions with a confidence line and one next step.
facts: About 235 smoke tests before each deploy
outcome: Six colleagues asked it about 105 questions, and one of its payout recommendations went live in an affiliate network.

hero.alt: A Slack thread. Someone asks Scout why revenue is down today. Scout replies that revenue is tracking 14% below its usual Tuesday, lists what is driving it and what is not the problem, gives one action, and closes with a confidence line: high, 4 weeks of data behind it.
hero.caption: A confidence line and one next step, every time.

story: Our revenue team already worked in Slack, so Scout lived there: @mention it in any channel and ask. When a colleague said a projected RPM looked wrong, Scout agreed and called its own number a model artifact.

Questions were what people came for. The scheduled posts, a morning pulse and weekly digests, drew almost no replies. I turned off an hourly monitor and removed a daily reminder that had gone about 137 days without a single answer.

calls.why: Every data answer carried a confidence line, and Scout said "Thin data" when fewer than 7 days or 100 sessions sat behind it.
If a publisher name could mean two accounts, it asked which one you meant.
In June a team lead rated an analyst's forecaster above Scout's. I folded its method in that day and kept it behind a backtest gate, out of users' sight.
Fifteen questions colleagues had actually asked decided which tool answered what, and which tools must not fire.

images.alt: A weekly Slack post titled New offers worth a look this week, listing two invented offers with payout, estimated RPM, a one-line reason and Add to Queue and Skip buttons.
images.caption: The weekly offer digest.

images.alt: A Slack alert titled Revenue velocity, publishers tracking down, flagging an invented publisher on pace to miss its month, with the likely cause and one thing to check.
images.caption: A velocity alert. Every screen uses Scout's card layout with invented data.
